Timeline::epoch_days¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::epoch_days() const

Project Instants Onto Fixed UTC Days¶

epoch_days() counts fixed 86,400-second intervals from the UTC Unix epoch and preserves the Timeline’s shape. It is a machine-time projection, not a local calendar-date extractor. For local calendar work, convert to the intended zone and use date(), day(), or dayofyear().

const auto times = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(
    {{-1LL, 0LL}, {1'999'999'999LL, pluss::Timeline::kNaT}});
std::cout << pluss::series::print(times.epoch_days()) << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ -1                    0 ⎤
⎣  0 -9223372036854775808 ⎦

One nanosecond before the epoch belongs to UTC day -1; both valid positive ticks shown are still in UTC day 0. Floor division supplies that boundary behavior. NaT remains Timeline::kNaT.

Local days can be 23 or 25 hours around offset transitions, whereas an epoch day here is always exactly 86,400 seconds. Do not use this method as a local date key unless that distinction is intentional.
